nodes.name: ZnSO₄-acetone electrolyte preparation
nodes.procedure: ZnSO₄ (2 M) with 20 v/v% acetone was prepared by mixing 20 vol% acetone with water and then adding 2 M ZnSO₄ salt into the above mixtures until the solutions became transparent and colorless.
nodes.source_text: Electrolyte Preparation: ZnSO₄ (2 M) electrolytes were prepared by dissolving 2 M ZnSO₄ salt into water to form transparent solutions. ZnSO₄ (2 M) with x v/v% acetone was prepared by mixing a certain volumetric ratio (10%, 20%, and 25%) of acetone and water and then adding 2 M ZnSO₄ salt into the above mixtures until the solutions became transparent.

nodes.source_text: the addition of 20 v/v% acetone to 2 M ZnSO4 electrolyte extends the lifespan of Zn//Zn symmetric cells from ≈12 to ≈800 h at both ultrahigh current density of 50 mA cm⁻² and areal capacity of 50 mAh cm⁻², with a high DOD of 73.5%. our battery accomplishes a superhigh CPC of 40 Ah cm⁻² at 50 mA cm⁻²

nodes.description: Zn-MnO2 full battery long-term cycling at 1 A/g
nodes.source_text: Long-term stability of both batteries was analyzed under a low current density of 1 A g⁻¹ (Figure 5e). The ZM-ace batteries deliver capacities of 155.2 and 144.9 mAh g⁻¹ at the initial and final state along with a capacity retention of 94.2%
When cycled at 1 A g⁻¹ under 40°C, the capacity of ZM-ace battery attains 170 mAh g⁻¹ and 98.8% capacity is retained after 1000 cycles

nodes.evidence_snippet: smooth surfaces with densely deposited Zn are maintained in ZnSO4-ace at all test conditions (Figure 3a-c). In sharp contrast, the anode surface becomes rough and porous, with apparent irregular Zn dendrites (Figure 3e-g).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows (002) plane dominant for cycled Zn foil in ZnSO4-ace with no Zn4SO4(OH)6·xH2O by-product peaks, while ZnSO4 shows (100) plane strongest and by-product peaks at 13.7° and 16.7°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We further characterize the plating products in the two electrolytes after 50 cycles by X-ray diffraction (XRD) spectroscopy (Figure 3k). Apparently, the evolution of H2 in ZnSO4 is associated with the generation of Zn4SO4(OH)6·xH2O by-products, as verified by the two pronounced peaks at 13.7° and 16.7°. In comparison, no characteristic peak of Zn4SO4(OH)6·xH2O can be found in ZnSO4-ace.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of Zn foil after 50 cycles shows C 1s peaks for C-C and C=O, and single S 2p peak for SO4^2-, indicating no SEI layer (ZnCO3 or ZnS) formed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To characterize whether solid electrolyte interface (SEI) is formed during cycling, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) is performed. According to the XPS results of Zn foil after 50 cycles in symmetric batteries, two peaks representing C-C and C=O can be observed in C 1s spectra, and only one peak representing SO4^2- can be found in S 2p spectra, suggesting no SEI layer (ZnCO3 or ZnS) is formed on Zn anode (Figure S15, Supporting Information).
